=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

## Key buyer-side concerns and push-back

### 1. Bluefen consent — **Completion condition must be robust**
**Issue:** Bluefen represents approximately **$3.6m / 30% of FY26 revenue**. The data room does not contain final written consent or proof that its conditions have been met. Seller’s statement that consent is “addressed” is not enough.

**Push back:**
- Make valid, unconditional Bluefen consent a **Buyer-benefit CP**, not merely a reasonable-endeavours covenant.
- Require delivery before Completion of:
  - consent in form satisfactory to Buyer;
  - evidence that every condition to consent has been satisfied or irrevocably waived;
  - confirmation that no termination, repricing, reduced scope, adverse amendment or default arises from Completion.
- Give Buyer a termination right if the CP is not satisfied by a long-stop date, without liability.
- If Seller will not accept a CP, require a substantial **specific indemnity / escrow / price adjustment**, reflecting the risk to 30% of revenue. A generic warranty claim regime is not adequate.

### 2. Riverlark debt and security — **must be discharged at Completion**
**Issue:** The company is being sold debt-free/cash-free, but approximately **$3.2m** remains outstanding and Seller proposes a release “following Completion.” That leaves Buyer owning a company with debt and potentially encumbered assets/shares at Completion.

**Push back:**
- Require the Riverlark facility to be repaid **at Completion from Seller’s proceeds**.
- Require delivery at Completion of:
  - irrevocable pay-off letter and funds-flow direction;
  - releases of all security, guarantees and related claims;
  - authority for Buyer to lodge and procure removal of PPSR/security registrations;
  - a post-Completion undertaking backed by an escrow/retention if releases cannot technically be registered that day.
- Exclude Riverlark debt, interest, break costs, discharge fees and security-release costs from any permitted debt or Buyer responsibility.
- Do not permit Completion against an undertaking merely to procure release later.

### 3. Liability limitations — **Seller’s proposed regime is too broad**
**Issue:** Seller seeks a 20% cap ($4.8m), 18-month survival, thresholds, and application of all limitations/exclusive-remedy/non-reliance provisions to “all Claims.” This could improperly capture title, tax, fraud, pre-Completion liabilities, specific indemnities and equitable remedies.

**Push back:**
- Limit the 20% cap, $25,000 de minimis, $250,000 deductible basket and 18-month period to ordinary **business warranties only**.
- Ensure each threshold operates on a **per-claim basis**, with related claims aggregated; prevent artificial splitting of claims.
- Seek a **tipping basket** (once exceeded, all loss is recoverable), rather than Seller’s deductible basket. At minimum, negotiate a materially lower basket.
- Preserve claims for:
  - title, capacity and authority;
  - tax;
  - fraud, fraudulent concealment, wilful misconduct and deliberate breach;
  - indemnities, including Bluefen/Riverlark/Ironquay and known matters;
  - leakage, debt/cash and completion-account/price-adjustment claims;
  - restrictive covenants and post-Completion covenants;
  - equitable relief and debt claims.
- A 20% cap is commercially thin given the identified risks. Seek a higher business-warranty cap, with separate and fuller recourse for the above carve-outs.

### 4. Fundamental warranties — **cannot share the general cap and 18-month limit**
**Issue:** Seller proposes subjecting title and capacity warranties to the general regime “for administrative simplicity.” This is unacceptable for a 100% share acquisition.

**Push back:**
- Title, capacity, authority, due execution, no encumbrances and ownership of all shares should be:
  - capped at **100% of purchase price** (at minimum);
  - subject to a substantially longer limitation period, preferably statutory limitation periods;
  - not subject to de minimis, basket, knowledge, data-room disclosure, exclusive-remedy or general limitation provisions.
- Obtain a specific warranty that all shares are fully paid, free of encumbrances and transferable, and that no person has options, conversion rights, pre-emption rights or other rights to acquire securities.

### 5. General disclosure — **reject data-room and public-records dumping**
**Issue:** Disclosure Letter clause 1 purports to disclose every fact “contained or referred to” in the entire indexed data room, statutory registers and public records. This is broad, uncertain, and shifts Seller’s disclosure burden to Buyer.

**Push back:**
- Delete general disclosure of the entire data room, public registers and materials “referred to” in documents.
- Disclosure should be effective only if it is:
  - expressly identified against the relevant warranty;
  - fair, specific and sufficiently detailed to identify the nature and scope of the exception and likely consequences;
  - in a final, closed, immutable data room indexed and agreed at signing.
- The disclosure should not qualify title, capacity, tax, fraud, specific indemnities, completion mechanics, or any matter expressly warranted to be true at Completion.
- Require Seller to warrant that the disclosure letter and data room are complete, accurate and not misleading by omission in material respects.
- Preserve Buyer rights for matters that are incompletely disclosed, where the Seller knows material facts not disclosed, and for material changes between signing and Completion.

### 6. Buyer knowledge / constructive knowledge — **delete**
**Issue:** Seller proposes no claim for anything Buyer or advisers knew, including matters “discoverable” from data room/public records. This imports a sweeping constructive-knowledge test and nullifies warranties.

**Push back:**
- Delete the provision. Warranties should allocate risk notwithstanding Buyer diligence.
- If any knowledge qualifier is unavoidable, it should be limited to:
  - Buyer’s **actual knowledge**;
  - of specifically named senior deal-team individuals only;
  - as at signing;
  - based on written information that clearly and fairly identifies the relevant breach and its material consequences.
- Exclude imputed, constructive, adviser and “discoverable” knowledge. No duty to investigate should arise.

### 7. Ironquay IP — **specific indemnity must cover ownership/use risk, not merely one invoice**
**Issue:** SOW3 project materials transfer only after cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. There is an apparent **$180,000** outstanding, no receipt and no confirmatory assignment. The company may lack title to important IP, potentially affecting its ability to operate or commercialise its product.

**Push back:**
- Require, before Completion:
  - payment evidence acceptable to Buyer;
  - a direct assignment/confirmatory assignment of all SOW3 project materials and related IP;
  - moral-rights consents and waivers;
  - confirmation of no lien, retention right, licence restriction or infringement claim.
- Expand the indemnity to cover all losses arising from any failure of title, licence, assignment, use or exploitation of Ironquay-delivered IP—not only payment of the identified SOW3 amount.
- The indemnity should be uncapped or separately capped, survive beyond general warranty limitations, and not be subject to knowledge/disclosure/basket restrictions.
- Retain an amount sufficient to cover the risk until documentary IP title is resolved.

### 8. Export/privacy incident — **material issue requiring a closing deliverable and protection**
**Issue:** DD-006 concerns a potentially unauthorised external disclosure involving approximately 1,240 personal-information records. The scope, access, regulatory-notification position and loss exposure remain unknown. Seller’s characterisation as merely preliminary/non-material is not a basis to accept the risk.

**Push back:**
- Require a full incident report before Completion covering:
  - data types, affected individuals and systems;
  - whether the recipient accessed, downloaded, retained or further disclosed data;
  - containment, deletion certification and forensic evidence;
  - legal assessment under the Privacy Act and Notifiable Data Breaches scheme;
  - communications with affected persons, regulators and customers.
- Require Seller to complete all appropriate pre-Completion investigation, containment and notifications, subject to Buyer consultation where legally permissible.
- Obtain a standalone indemnity for all pre-Completion incident-related liabilities: investigations, response and remediation costs, notification, regulatory action, claims, penalties to the extent legally indemnifiable, customer concessions and reputational/customer remediation.
- Require a no-material-adverse-change / no-new-material-incident bring-down warranty at Completion.
- Consider an escrow or retention pending final incident findings.

### 9. Completion bonuses — **Seller must bear all costs**
**Issue:** The disclosed conditional bonuses total **$420,000**, are omitted from the funds flow, and payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are unknown. These are likely Completion-triggered liabilities that Buyer would inherit.

**Push back:**
- Treat all Completion bonuses and every related cost—including superannuation, payroll tax, workers compensation, leave effects, withholding and administrative costs—as **Seller leakage / Seller transaction costs**, not company liabilities.
- Require payment at or before Completion through the agreed funds flow, or an escrowed amount sufficient for the gross cost plus on-costs.
- Obtain a specific indemnity for all amounts arising from these arrangements.
- Require a complete schedule of each beneficiary, gross amount, conditions, payment timing, on-costs and any retention/continued-employment treatment.
- Ensure payments do not create retention, change-of-control, discrimination or employee-relations claims against the Buyer group.

### 10. Tax protection — **general warranty regime is inadequate**
**Issue:** Seller says tax is “settled” under general limitations. That is inappropriate for pre-Completion tax liabilities, especially where identified bonuses and transaction arrangements may create payroll-tax, income-tax and withholding exposures.

**Push back:**
- Include a customary **Tax Deed / Tax Covenant** covering all pre-Completion tax liabilities, including penalties, interest and reasonable costs.
- It should cover taxes arising from:
  - pre-Completion periods;
  - Completion, sale-related steps and Seller-directed transactions;
  - employee bonuses and other transaction payments;
  - failures to withhold, report or pay payroll tax, superannuation or employment taxes.
- Tax claims should have a longer survival period (normally until the relevant assessment/amendment period expires, plus a buffer), no general basket/de minimis, and separate recourse/cap.
- Require delivery of tax returns, tax payment evidence and a tax clearance/status schedule.

### 11. IP warranties — **do not leave under general regime**
**Issue:** The Ironquay issue demonstrates potential defects in ownership of material IP. General IP warranties subject to 20% cap, disclosure dumping and 18 months are insufficient.

**Push back:**
- Strengthen warranties that the company owns or has valid, transferable, perpetual rights to all IP necessary to conduct the business as currently conducted and planned.
- Cover contractor assignments, open-source compliance, licences, infringement/non-infringement claims, domain names, source code, repositories and employee/consultant IP assignments.
- Carve core IP-title issues out of general disclosure/knowledge limitations and give them a separate cap and longer survival period.
- Make delivery of Ironquay title documentation a Completion deliverable.

### 12. Supplier renewals — **obtain facts and prevent undisclosed leakage/commitments**
**Issue:** Three related renewals total **$330,000**, but the disclosure does not confirm whether they are unavoidable, terminable, already accrued, or ordinary course. Seller’s bare assertion that they are ordinary-course costs does not resolve the risk.

**Push back:**
- Require copies, status and commercial detail for each renewal: term, termination rights, committed spend, timing, payment status, services, related-party status and any change-of-control provisions.
- Require confirmation that there are no other material supplier commitments or prepayments outside ordinary course.
- If the contracts create unusual or non-terminable commitments, address them through a price adjustment, leakage treatment, specific indemnity or CP, as appropriate.
- Include an interim covenant preventing material new commitments, renewals, prepayments or changes to supplier arrangements without Buyer consent.

### 13. Office lease and Mossvale — **confirm no consent/default risk**
**Issue:** The disclosures are framed negatively: they say material does not describe a consent requirement. That is not affirmative confirmation that no consent, notice, default or termination risk exists.

**Push back:**
- Require affirmative warranties and a contract/lease schedule identifying all change-of-control, notice, consent, termination and price-change provisions.
- Obtain needed notices, waivers or consents before Completion where the documents require them.
- Require the Seller to confirm no counterparty has asserted a breach, termination right or adverse amendment arising from the transaction.

### 14. Funds flow and debt-free/cash-free mechanics — **fully document the economic deal**
**Issue:** The draft’s lack of separate bonus treatment and post-Completion Riverlark discharge raises concern that the funds flow does not actually implement debt-free/cash-free economics.

**Push back:**
- Agree a detailed Completion Statement and funds-flow schedule showing:
  - purchase price;
  - permitted cash and permitted debt definitions;
  - Riverlark repayment and all discharge costs;
  - all Seller transaction expenses;
  - bonus and employment-related payments/on-costs;
  - any escrow, retention or deferred amounts;
  - recipient, amount and payment timing for every Completion payment.
- Define debt broadly to include accrued interest, break fees, guarantees, security, finance leases, shareholder liabilities and transaction-linked obligations.
- Include a post-Completion true-up/audit mechanism and a clear priority of rights alongside warranty claims.

---

## Recommended negotiation priorities

1. **Do not complete without Bluefen consent/conditions resolved and Riverlark repaid with security releases.** These are immediate value and balance-sheet risks.
2. **Secure documentary Ironquay IP title** or retain/escrow against a broad IP indemnity.
3. **Obtain specific protection for the privacy/export incident**, including investigation, notification/remediation obligations and an indemnity/retention.
4. **Make the $420,000 bonuses and all on-costs Seller-funded**, reflected expressly in funds flow or escrow.
5. **Reject wholesale data-room/public-record disclosure and constructive Buyer knowledge.**
6. **Ring-fence fundamental, tax, IP, debt/leakage, indemnity and fraud claims from general caps, thresholds, survival periods and exclusive-remedy provisions.**
7. **Require a proper tax covenant and adequate tax survival period.**
8. **Update disclosure and bring-down warranties at Completion**, coupled with a right not to complete for material new issues.

Overall, Seller’s package attempts to place known, material pre-Completion risks inside a heavily restricted general warranty regime while also treating the entire data room as disclosure. Buyer should resist that structure: the identified matters require Completion deliverables, specific indemnities and/or economic protection, rather than reliance on a $4.8m, 18-month general warranty claim regime.

- Require confirmation that there are no other material supplier commitments or prepayments outside ordinary course.
- If the contracts create unusual or non-terminable commitments, address them through a price adjustment, leakage treatment, specific indemnity or CP, as appropriate.
- Include an interim covenant preventing material new commitments, renewals, prepayments or changes to supplier arrangements without Buyer consent.

### 13. Office lease and Mossvale — **confirm no consent/default risk**
**Issue:** The disclosures are framed negatively: they say material does not describe a consent requirement. That is not affirmative confirmation that no consent, notice, default or termination risk exists.

**Push back:**
- Require affirmative warranties and a contract/lease schedule identifying all change-of-control, notice, consent, termination and price-change provisions.
- Obtain needed notices, waivers or consents before Completion where the documents require them.
- Require the Seller to confirm no counterparty has asserted a breach, termination right or adverse amendment arising from the transaction.

### 14. Funds flow and debt-free/cash-free mechanics — **fully document the economic deal**
**Issue:** The draft’s lack of separate bonus treatment and post-Completion Riverlark discharge raises concern that the funds flow does not actually implement debt-free/cash-free economics.

**Push back:**
- Agree a detailed Completion Statement and funds-flow schedule showing:
  - purchase price;
  - permitted cash and permitted debt definitions;
  - Riverlark repayment and all discharge costs;
  - all Seller transaction expenses;
  - bonus and employment-related payments/on-costs;
  - any escrow, retention or deferred amounts;
  - recipient, amount and payment timing for every Completion payment.
- Define debt broadly to include accrued interest, break fees, guarantees, security, finance leases, shareholder liabilities and transaction-linked obligations.
- Include a post-Completion true-up/audit mechanism and a clear priority of rights alongside warranty claims.

## Recommended negotiation priorities

1. **Do not complete without Bluefen consent/conditions resolved and Riverlark repaid with security releases.** These are immediate value and balance-sheet risks.
2. **Secure documentary Ironquay IP title** or retain/escrow against a broad IP indemnity.
3. **Obtain specific protection for the privacy/export incident**, including investigation, notification/remediation obligations and an indemnity/retention.
4. **Make the $420,000 bonuses and all on-costs Seller-funded**, reflected expressly in funds flow or escrow.
5. **Reject wholesale data-room/public-record disclosure and constructive Buyer knowledge.**
6. **Ring-fence fundamental, tax, IP, debt/leakage, indemnity and fraud claims from general caps, thresholds, survival periods and exclusive-remedy provisions.**
7. **Require a proper tax covenant and adequate tax survival period.**
8. **Update disclosure and bring-down warranties at Completion**, coupled with a right not to complete for material new issues.

Overall, Seller’s package attempts to place known, material pre-Completion risks inside a heavily restricted general warranty regime while also treating the entire data room as disclosure. Buyer should resist that structure: the identified matters require Completion deliverables, specific indemnities and/or economic protection, rather than reliance on a $4.8m, 18-month general warranty claim regime.
